Vote - AcceptText - The corrections look fine to me. I slightly prefer Καστορίων over Καστορίω in l. 16, but would not change the order of the alternative readings.
Vote - AcceptText - I find both new readings convincing. I would slightly prefer Καστορ̣ί̣ῳ̣, since I do not see the same little "Knick" for the ny as in the case of Καστορίων in line 18.

Submit - line 16: the reading Καστορίωνι is not tenable, because there is no iota at the end of the name. Καστορίῳ (cf. omega in Σεουήρῳ at beginning of the same line) or Καστορίων (cf. ων at end of the name in line 18) are both possible readings of the end of the name. Either way, Καστορίωνι would be the conventional form (hence the reg tag). After this name, the ed.pr. has π̣υ̣ρ̣ο̣ῦ̣, which is also impossible. δεκ just before αρταβ/ is quite clear, and αποδεκ/ readily recognizable, which gives Severus's and Kastorion's titles. A faint diagonal stroke of abbreviation is visible above and to the right of kappa. Omission of the word for the grain is not unheard of (cf. P.Cair. Isid. 57.16ff.). The link to CSAD in HGV does not work. You can find the image here: http://ipap.csad.ox.ac.uk/PSI-bw/300dpi/PSI.VII.820A.jpg. Note, too, that line ends of a column at the far left of the papyrus were not included in the ed.pr. I plan to enter them at a later date. Line 22: I've entered a BL correction.
